#### story-161 — plan review findings reach the first executor, which can extend the card's test map   [done]
Context: note 6fcc0b70. A consuming project reports story-093 and story-095 each stopped after plan review found test or file names absent from the card. Checked at main: spawn.py builds the executor prompt before the planner and plan reviewer and rebuilds it only on a replan; the first executor therefore receives neither the review disposition nor a path to it from that stage. plan-reviewer.md flags missing AC checks in Verify but may edit only the plan; plan_review.py refuses a card edit. EXECUTOR.md permits Files growth and says to run the card's exact Verify, but says nothing about tests newly identified in the reviewed plan. ready.card_growth already accepts additive Files and an appended ` && ` Verify command without reminting; other card edits refuse. The consumer's native-permissions fake prebuild test is a repeatable check; its one real prebuild and phone-call device run are execution evidence, not automatic pre-push commands. Do not bake those project-specific examples into shipped prose.
Decision: keep the reviewer plan-only. Deliver its findings to the executor on the FIRST run and on resume, with a readable path under the shared data root; say explicitly that the executor runs diagnostic tests from the reviewed plan, extends Files for touched paths and appends repeatable AC checks to Verify before handback. Give it the absolute card path and a runnable locked edit route. work.py edit-card already applies a one-card candidate under plan.lock with digest/status preconditions, while spawn holds only a per-story resume lock; reuse that mechanism if it suffices, rather than teaching a direct overwrite of shared plan.md. Human-only acceptance and changes to AC or scope go to the lead. A reviewer writing the card would cross the current review-state guard and may force replanning; that complexity is not needed to remove this stop.

#### story-162 — a moved plugin still prints an executable recovery command   [done]
Context: note c2b49e89. This session's first SessionStart measurement was 9,012/9,500 bytes with a move notice; the slate reviewer measured 8,998 bytes from this checkout root without a move notice. The user's moved-cache session received `recover: session_start.py recover`. session_start.py:459-467 deliberately drops the `python3 <installed-root>/scripts/` prefix when refresh_env reports a root move; the environment notice separately names the new root. The lead in this session located the script in the source repo to recover, a step a consuming project's lead should not have to infer. The full `--- END project content ---` closes a trust boundary and saves only about 24 bytes if reduced to `END`; keep it. The output budget and full constraint delivery remain hard properties.
Decision: make the banner's recover field a command executable as printed under normal and moved roots. Keep the data-root field and explicit data fence. The move notice repeats the current plugin root that the full command will name; shorten that duplication and, if needed, remove the low-value `scripts:` field. The path-envelope fixture has 47 spare bytes today and the full command costs about 127 extra at its 110-character root, so the net reduction must be at least 80 bytes. Measure it, not a guessed saving.

#### free-2026-09-28-backmerge-round — trunk merged into a reviewed sprint costs no round where it touched nothing the sprint wrote   [done]
Context: GitHub issue #154, mapped at 42efdaf and against legacy2's sprint j1b (data root 579940124c7d). The issue's premise holds only AFTER a recorded round. Round 1 reads `merge-base(trunk, HEAD)..HEAD` (sprint_review.py:60, bookkeep.fork_point :168-209, sprint_bundle.py:85,91), so a backmerge before round 1 is already free. After a round, the confirming bundle reads `shown_sha..HEAD` (sprint_review.py:95) and land's `_coverage_refusal` (sprint_land.py:202-280) diffs `shown..head` two-dot: every file a trunk backmerge brought in counts as uncovered, and the peer commits are `reviewer_strays` (review.py:237-244), so land refuses "the review did not cover HEAD" and owes a round over peers' already-released work. The story leg already solved this: overlap.land_refusal (:48-92) records `review_base` and accepts forward-only base motion when `_files(recorded..base) & _files(base..HEAD)` is empty (tests/test_close_land_rounds.py:187,197,206). The sprint marker records no `review_base` (sprint_review_resume.py:247-283 writes rounds with reviewed_head/shown_sha only). j1b would still have owed its round under this card (7 shared files, 3 conflicts, a trunk-brought `.xp/system.md` gate file, a lead code commit a97699be) — the gain is for the disjoint case, which parallel clones hit whenever a peer releases between a sprint's review and its land.
Decision: record the trunk merge base on every completed sprint round, and at sprint land exempt from the `shown..head` delta exactly the paths that (a) changed on trunk between the recorded base and today's merge base, (b) are NOT changed by the sprint at HEAD against today's merge base (so HEAD's content equals trunk's), and (c) were NOT changed by the sprint in the round it recorded (`recorded_base..shown`) — (c) is what stops a take-theirs conflict resolution from silently discarding reviewed sprint work. Forward-only: a recorded base that is not an ancestor of today's merge base gets no exemption. Gate files are never exempt, whoever brought them. Everything else in the delta keeps today's rules (reviewer-own, `.xp/` prose, release bump), and anything left still refuses. Land prints the exempted paths and the trunk range as their own labelled line, never folded into the reviewer's. A confirming round that IS owed reads the delta minus those exempt paths, and names the trunk range it left out. Put the path computation in one shared function beside land_refusal's so story and sprint rules cannot drift; before relying on it, construct the take-theirs case against the STORY rule — if land_refusal accepts a resolution that drops reviewed story work, file a bug with that red falsifier (do not widen this card to fix it).

- Given the same backmerge plus a lead commit to any non-exempt code path, or trunk motion touching a file the sprint also changed (at HEAD or in the reviewed round), or a merge resolved take-theirs over a reviewed sprint change, or a trunk-brought gate file, Then land refuses as today and names the uncovered paths. Each arm is fault-injected against the exemption with that arm's check removed.
- Given a round recorded before this change (no base in the marker), a recorded base that is not an ancestor of today's merge base, or a stale/diverged local trunk, Then no exemption applies and the existing refusal (or fork_point's stale-trunk refusal) stands — missing base is a distinct state from a base that moved (constraint 15).
- Given a confirming round is owed after such a backmerge, Then its bundle excludes the exempt trunk-only paths and names the excluded trunk range; round 1 bundles are unchanged.
- Given deterministic clearance of bound blockers, Then no trunk exemption applies there (it already refuses pending trunk and moved HEAD).
- Given a scratch consuming project on `release: sprint` with a peer free-patch landing on trunk after the sprint's recorded round, Then walk review → backmerge → land (dry run is enough to reach coverage) with the installed-shape scripts and record what was observed (constraint 12).
Close review: deep — an exemption that admits a silently dropped or unreviewed change is a false green over the release; the refusal boundaries are the product.
NEGATIVE SPACE: no exemption for gate files, conflict resolutions, or lead commits; no change to round 1's range, to the full-tier trial merge, or to release-bump handling; nothing recorded as a work.md record for an exempted trunk range (land output is the report). No auto-backmerge.
